quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from flat mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are common on motorcycles. They show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles coming toward you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What is a difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield prevents eye watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good replacement for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When you sit on a motorcycle:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
Stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should be slightly bent when you hold the handgrips.

questions.question: In which lane position are motorcyclists usually easiest to see?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car because it puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions change.

questions.question: In general, what is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Good riders change their position as conditions change.

questions.question: When you and another vehicle reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight so the other vehicle knows to go.
Go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Where should a motorcyclist ride in a lane when being passed?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When someone is passing you from behind or from the front, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing driver is dangerous for both of you.

questions.question: A wobble, or sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars, is usually caused by:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight.
Front wheel not tightened properly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars suddenly shake side to side. Most wobbles happen because of wrong loading, bad accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris usually collect in which part of a lane?

options.text: The left side
The middle
The right side

questions.correctAnswerText: The middle
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You can go over the speed limit until the pass is done.
You can ignore no passing zone markings if you started the pass in a legal zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done within the speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When reacting to a hazard in the road, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers what you are doing.
Change your speed as needed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you are doing by using your horn, lights, and signals. Change your speed to match the situation. Move to a different lane position if needed.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must stop completely.
You can go through carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop completely.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a green arrow before turning in that direction.

questions.question: What should you do when lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
Go slowly and carefully.
Turn around and use a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to drive around a train.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol level (BAC)?

options.text: How much alcohol is consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often a person usually drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person usually drinks
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on your body weight, how much alcohol you drink, and how fast you drink it. It is safest to never ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will probably lose control.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if the bike stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be used during daylight.
Be used without a driver license.
Be used with any type of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used with any type of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: The center of a lane sometimes has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Should always be avoided.
Usually gives enough grip unless it is wet.
Should only be used if another vehicle is in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually gives enough grip unless it is wet.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the center of the road usually provides enough grip for safe riding when dry. When it rains, the strip becomes slippery. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of your lane.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left side of the lane, next to the center line.
On the right side of the lane, next to the edge.
It depends on the road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose the position that gives you the best view and the most space around you. Change your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers what traffic laws apply in this area. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean toward the direction you are turning.
Slow down while turning.
Turn using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean toward the direction you are turning.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of your turn. Slow down before you start the turn.
